prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.62
  gal: 0.38
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_E:
Summary of key proposals and commitments (ideology removed)

Economy and public finances
- Eliminate most of the structural deficit within a Parliament; emergency Budget within 50 days; create an independent Office for Budget Responsibility; immediate £6bn savings; one‑year public sector pay freeze (excluding the lowest‑paid); reduce Whitehall and quango costs; cut ministers’ pay; reduce MPs by 10%.
- Modify 2011 National Insurance plans to reduce costs for employees under £35k and employers; lower and simplify business taxes (corporation tax to 25%, small companies to 20%) funded by relieving complex allowances; establish a five‑year corporate tax roadmap and an Office of Tax Simplification.
- Refocus R&D tax credits on hi‑tech SMEs; strengthen STEM, research stability and university‑business links; improve export support; promote saving (restore earnings link to state pension, auto‑enrolment) and end the effective annuity requirement at 75.
- Strengthen consumer finance protection (new agency, free national advice service, clearer credit card rules) and help manage unsecured debt.

Jobs, skills, welfare, immigration
- Single Work Programme for all unemployed; reassess incapacity claims; earlier, tailored, payment‑by‑results support; sanctions for refusal; community work placements; NI holiday for new firms’ first 10 hires; expand apprenticeships, work pairings and careers advice; free colleges from central control; 10,000 extra university places and HE funding reform.
- Set an annual limit on non‑EU economic migration; transitional controls for new EU members; English test for spouses; tighten student visas and require bonds for certain institutions.

Infrastructure, regions, enterprise
- High‑speed rail linking major cities; no new runways at Heathrow, Stansted, Gatwick; rail franchise reform; consult on a Fair Fuel Stabiliser; superfast broadband via infrastructure sharing; replace RDAs with local enterprise partnerships; let councils keep part of business rate growth; open government procurement to SMEs.

Public services, transparency, banking
- Publish all central and local spending over low thresholds, senior salaries, and contracts; expand open data rights; support employee‑led mutuals to run services; reduce quangos; improve procurement governance.
- Bank levy; place prudential supervision with the central bank; curb risky activities, promote competition, and expand affordable SME credit.

Environment and energy
- Cut emissions 80% by 2050; 10% cut in central government emissions within 12 months; Green Investment Bank; carbon price floor; Green Deal (up to ~£6,500 per home); smart grid/meters; new nuclear (no subsidy); four CCS plants; offshore grid and marine energy; expand small‑scale and district heating.
- Protect habitats and marine zones; oppose whaling and ivory trade; criminalise illegal timber imports; plant up to 1m trees; reform fisheries and agriculture; tackle bTB (including targeted badger control); supermarket ombudsman; honest food labelling.

Families, health, education, social care
- Recognise marriage and civil partnerships in tax; end couple penalty in tax credits over time; two‑year council tax freeze; extend flexible working and shared parental leave; curb marketing to children; refocus Sure Start and add 4,200 health visitors.
- Real‑terms NHS funding growth; patient choice across qualified providers; GP‑led commissioning; publish outcomes; 24/7 urgent care and extended GP hours; protect local maternity/A&E where viable; Cancer Drugs Fund; new dentistry contract; personal budgets for long‑term conditions; support carers; voluntary insurance to protect homes from care costs; public health funding with a “health premium.”
- Raise teacher quality and discipline; phonics with a reading check at six; more rigorous curriculum/exams; technical academies; reform league tables; pupil premium; expand academies/new schools; protect special schools; faster intervention in failing schools.

Crime, borders, civil liberties, local power
- Tougher alcohol licensing; instant sanctions for ASB; prison sentences for knife crimes; extend magistrates’ powers; victim information; reduce police paperwork; directly elected local oversight of policing; monthly local crime data; Border Police Force; expand prison capacity; payment‑by‑results rehabilitation; abstinence‑based drug orders; temporary bans on new “legal highs.”
- Scrap ID cards and central databases; limit DNA retention; reform criminal records; replace broad surveillance powers; strengthen data protection.
- Recall for MPs; cap big donations and tighten lobbying rules; citizen petitions to trigger debates; equalise constituencies; individual voter registration; backbench control of Commons time.
- Neighbourhood‑led planning; abolish regional targets; local referendums and vetoes on high council tax; community right to buy/run services; elected mayors in largest cities; general power of competence for councils.

Foreign, defence, aid
- National Security Council; Strategic Defence and Security Review; homeland defence command; sustain mission in Afghanistan; renew nuclear deterrent; cut MOD running costs ~25%; procurement reform; enhance support for service personnel and families.
- Active global engagement, alliances and human rights emphasis; EU “referendum lock” on future power transfers; no Euro adoption; seek return of specific powers.
- Legislate to spend 0.7% of national income on aid by 2013; full aid transparency; end aid to certain middle‑income countries; focus on basics and women/children/disabled; at least £500m/year on malaria; support trade, property rights and a Stabilisation & Reconstruction Force; climate‑smart, greener export support; promote a Pan‑African free trade area.

TEXT_F:
Summary of proposals and commitments

- Economy and public finances: Support the recovery before tightening from 2011–12; more than halve the deficit by 2014 via growth, fairer tax increases (including National Insurance), cuts to lower-priority spend, £15–20bn annual efficiencies, asset sales, a 1% public‑sector pay cap (2011–13), and public‑sector pension reforms. Protect frontline spending on childcare, schools, the NHS and policing.

- Banking and industry: Tougher bank regulation, capital and “living wills,” a global levy, stronger competition, and disposal of state stakes. Create UK Finance for Growth (£4bn) to channel capital to SMEs and high‑tech firms; expand R&D tax credits, capital allowances and a “patent box.” Tighten takeover rules (two‑thirds shareholder support) and promote employee ownership.

- Jobs, welfare and skills: Future Jobs Fund (200,000 jobs); youth job/training guarantee at six months, mandatory by ten; guaranteed work after two years’ unemployment. Minimum wage to rise at least with average earnings; £40/week Better Off in Work guarantee; expand apprenticeships, technician routes and Skills Accounts; reform incapacity benefits with reassessments and more support to work.

- Infrastructure: High Speed Rail from London to Midlands and North with through‑services to Scotland; Crossrail completion; key rail electrification; motorway hard‑shoulder running; no national road pricing; a third runway at Heathrow with conditions. Universal broadband via a modest landline levy; Green Investment Bank; modernised energy grid.

- Housing and consumer finance: Two‑year stamp duty holiday for first‑time buyers up to £250k (funded by 5% rate over £1m); more affordable and social homes; council house building enabled; stronger repossession protections; private rented sector standards and a national landlord register. Transform the Post Office into a People’s Bank; universal right to a basic bank account; support for affordable credit and action on high‑cost lending; portable account/ISA numbers.

- Education: Increase frontline funding for Sure Start, childcare, schools and 16–19; expand free nursery places (age two) and 15 hours for ages 3–4. One‑to‑one/small‑group catch‑up; personal tutors in secondary; powers to replace weak school leadership; growth of accredited school groups; fair admissions; pupil premium locally; strengthened SEN support. Participation to 18; major expansion of advanced apprenticeships; HE funding review with widened access.

- Health and care: Protect NHS spending; up to £20bn efficiencies reinvested. Patient guarantees: 18‑week treatment or funded private care; one‑week cancer test results; over‑40s health checks; choice of any qualified provider; more diagnostics; expanded psychological therapies; more care at home; personal care plans and budgets. Create a National Care Service: from 2011 free home care for highest needs; from 2014 cap residential costs after two years; long‑term move to comprehensive, free‑at‑point‑use care for eligible adults.

- Families and older people: A flexible paid “Father’s Month”; a £4/week Toddler Tax Credit; extend flexible working (including older workers); end default retirement at 65; re‑link Basic State Pension to earnings from 2012; expand low‑cost pension saving; NI credits for caregiving grandparents.

- Policing, justice and immigration: Maintain police/PCSO numbers; neighbourhood policing with accountability; performance “report cards” and powers to replace failing leadership. Early intervention for troubled families; faster, stronger action on anti‑social behaviour, including victim injunctions; expand Community Payback. Use of CCTV and DNA with safeguards; voluntary ID scheme; court and legal aid efficiencies; stronger victim support. Control immigration via a points‑based system, tougher English requirements, stronger borders, and focusing access to entitlements on citizens/permanent residents.

- Environment and rural: Aim for ~40% low‑carbon electricity by 2020 (renewables, nuclear, CCS); Green Investment Bank; home “pay‑as‑you‑save” upgrades, smart meters; move toward zero waste; expand habitats, protect Green Belt, increase woodland; fairer food chain (supermarkets ombudsman), clearer origin labelling; CAP and fisheries reforms.

- Culture, sport and communities: Deliver 2012 Olympics legacy; expand school/community sport; enable supporter trusts to buy stakes in clubs; maintain free museum entry and arm’s‑length governance; protect post offices and pubs; uphold BBC independence; support film and video games industries.

- Governance, local power and global role: Referenda on Alternative Vote and a reformed, elected second chamber; fixed‑term parliaments; lobbying register and tighter rules on outside jobs; recall for serious misconduct; expand open data. Stronger local government powers and city‑region devolution; urban transport upgrades; keep council tax rises low. Afghanistan strategy focused on training and transition; Strategic Defence Review; maintain nuclear deterrent; improved support for forces and veterans. Active EU engagement; counter‑terrorism and non‑proliferation; commit 0.7% of national income to aid by 2013 in law; focus on health, education, water/sanitation, anti‑corruption; pursue reform of UN, IFIs, G8/G20 and NATO.

Judge whether TEXT_E or TEXT_F aligns more closely with this profile.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_E" | "TEXT_F"
}
